Posted June 4, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan
See
 Judge Rules Against Defense On All Major Motions In McCormick/McWilliams Case; Ruling On Medical Necessity Defense Scheduled For October.
Selective Prosecution and Unequal Injustice. Special To MarijuanaNews

And for a 1999 story about Rosenthal codefendant Ken Hayes see
 More Unequal Injustice In California;
Raids on Medical Marijuana Supplies Hurt the Sick and Dying

The Narcocracy took a major hit today when Federal Judge Charles Breyer sentenced Ed Rosenthal to just one day (time served) for growing medical cannabis in California.
See
 Astonishing Editorial In New York Times Attacks Rosenthal Prosecution. Finally Taking The Issue Seriously?

However, one should note that he is also a convicted felon, and subject to regular urine testing that could be a death sentence for some patients, like Kubby and Tuck.
See
 Placer County: Still Crazy After All These Years. Kubby Hearings Offer New Evidence California Law Enforcement Still Fighting Medical Cannabis Law. Special Report to MarijuanaNews.com

Inasmuch as the case is getting international coverage, this sentence will be rightly interpreted as a defeat for the prohibitionists. I would have loved seeing the expression on John Walters face! Also, it will be interesting to see how it is reported in Canada, and in areas where there is no free press, like Washington, DC.
See
 How Does The Washington Post Play Catch-Up On The Rosenthal Case? Very Briefly.

It should also be noted that this case broke new ground for jury nullification. The jury gave the required verdict, but then embarrassed the judge and the system with an open rebellion. That is a victory for the people, the cannabis issues aside.

I am obviously pleased on many levels, but before people get too carried away with the cheering, we should note that this case and this sentence highlight not only what is wrong with cannabis prohibition, but also what is wrong with the cannabis reform movement, especially the medical cannabis movement.

First, we should not forget that Bryan Epis just began serving a ten-year federal sentence for running a cannabis buyers club in Chico, California. Steve McWilliams is appealing a six-month federal sentence for growing 21 plants.
See
 Federal Prosecution of Activist Steve McWilliams For Just 25 Plants Relevant to American Refugees In Canada. Being Outspoken Is The Real Crime. Being Deprived Of Medication Is The Real Punishment.

My friend Todd McCormick is going be in federal prison for another year or so, and has just been moved again, as a part of the sadistic system's so-called diesel therapy.

Todd's new address:
Todd McCormick
Inmate # 11071-112,
Phoenix FCI, 37910
North 45th Avenue,
Phoenix, AZ 85086

Please write to him. Think about how he must feel about this sentence.

And, oh yes, Peter McWilliams is still dead.
See
 The Murder of Peter McWilliams -- An Indictment, Not an Obituary by Richard Cowan

Then there are all the others that we have not even heard about.

But, also think about what this case says about our movement. Ed Rosenthal has received hundreds of thousands of dollars in support, even though he has a very affluent lifestyle. Where was the support for those who are not famous?

Others, like Steve Tuck, who had to flee to Canada, have been largely abandoned by the people who feed on the celebrity culture that confuses the famous with the truly heroic.
See
 Tuck Refugee Hearings End. The Facts Put Canada In Awkward Position. Catching A Nark In A Lie? Imagine That! News and Analysis by Richard Cowan.

The fact is that we have one set of laws for the rich and another for the poor, for those who know how to play the system, and another for those who do not, cannot or will not.

And the big financial supporters of the various medical cannabis initiatives have ignored the people whose lives have been destroyed because they thought that the laws meant what they say. Judge Breyer explained his reasoning today, The court finds the circumstances of the offense are highly unusual.,..What is significant for sentencing purposes is whether the defendant believed he was protected.

But all of the California defendants thought that they were protected.

I ask from time to time if the sick and dying have liberated us yet, but we really are using the neediest among us as canon fodder.

We are living in a time of moral chaos. Today's victory is a victory only if we build on it and use it to help those less fortunate.
